Air pollution

Environmental criminology in its two senses. Pollution as harm and offence (green criminology) - who bears the exposure from an emitting site and the burden it causes, by area and by income; and the environment as a driver of offending and victimisation, where exposure series are joined to crime counts by place and day. Dispersion models (Pasquill-Gifford sigmas, Briggs plume rise, the Gaussian plume and puff, a grid and a particle model), the concentration-response functions of PM2.5 and NO2, the attributable fraction, deaths avoided, the burden by area and the concentration index of exposure by income.

pgsig() briggs() gplume() gspuff() advdif2d() lagrprt() print(<advdif2d>) print(<lagrprt>)

Exposure and crime

Environmental criminology asks how the places and conditions in which people live and move shape offending and victimisation. These functions estimate the effect of a daily exposure such as air pollution on counts by place and day, with fixed effects, wind and inversion instruments, an irrelevant-day placebo and the upwind and downwind design, after Bondy, Roth and Sager (2020, Crime is in the air, Journal of the Association of Environmental and Resource Economists 7(3), doi:10.1086/707127) and Herrnstadt, Heyes, Muehlegger and Saberian (2019, Air pollution as a cause of violent crime; 2021, Air pollution and criminal activity, American Economic Journal - Applied Economics 13(4), doi:10.1257/app.20190091).

Environmental crime

Offences against the environment as the outcome: where, when and why pollution offences, illegal waste disposal and safety crimes are recorded, and how enforcement shapes the counts. The LMDI decomposition of a count over a Kaya identity, two-way fixed effects with an interaction and its checks, Pesaran’s CD test of a panel, difference and system GMM for dynamic panels, Wooldridge’s test of serial correlation and common correlated effects.

Write text as UTF-8, falling back to ASCII where it is not UTF-8

Shares

Each count as a share of its total, with Wilson intervals that stay inside 0 to 100.

shrs()
Share of a total, in percent

Categorical integrity

Category codes decoded and recoded by name, never by position, each recode proved by a cross-tabulation and checked against the counts a release published.

A factor with declared, verified levels

Decode a labelled import by its value labels

Prove a recode with a before/after cross-tabulation
vrfmrg()
Verify recoded counts against the counts a release published
xfrvrf()
Verify a categorical variable that crossed from one program to another

Region maps

Crosswalks from units (facilities, detachments, courts) to statistical regions, checked for soundness, against a published map and against a second route.

rgnmapintg()
Internal soundness of a region map
rgnmapcmp()
Compare a recomputed region map against a published one
rgnmapalt()
Check a region map against an independently derived assignment

Drift between releases

Has a table’s distribution moved between two periods or two releases? Check a new release of an agency’s published table against the last one before computing change from it.

drftks()
Two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test (C backend)
drftpsi()
Population stability index and Jensen-Shannon divergence (C backend)
drftchisq()
Chi-square test of a categorical column against a known distribution
drfthomog()
Chi-square test of homogeneity of two categorical samples

Change tables out

Period-over-period change tables labelled, summarised and written to CSV, TSV, JSON, Markdown, HTML and PDF for police services, corrections and courts alike; the delimited and JSON writers keep every digit and every code.

yoysmry()

Render a change table to HTML or PDF

Write a change table in the format its file name says

Describing a table

The look at a table before trusting it - the shape of every column, where the gaps are and whether they are random, which values dominate, which rows do not belong, and whether distinct groups differ.

Frequency table for one column
cortbl() print(<cortbl>)

Strongest pairwise correlations in a data frame

dstntst() print(<dstntst>)
Do distinct groups differ? A heterogeneity test before pooling

The energy an analysis used and the emissions of making it on the local grid, offline - modelled or measured, with the measured energy of other devices added, and every assumption listed.
